subtitle: UPDATE Jul 30, 17:08 BRT, 66 days to the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). THE PRICE ROSE AND THE POLLING DID NOT MOVE. Lula advances 1.00pp and returns to 63.50%, which TIES the top of the AFOS series for the third time (Jul 26, Jul 28 and now Jul 30) without exceeding it, and the gap over Flávio, flat at 23.95%, widens from +38.55pp to +39.55pp, sitting 0.25pp below the series maximum, the +39.80pp of Jul 26. THE DAY'S POLLING: PoderData/Aya of Jul 30 (n=2,400, field Jul 26 to 29, 2pp margin, 95% confidence, BR-07845/2026, telephone on mobile and landline, 677 municipalities across the 27 states) has Lula 41% to Flávio 35% in the first round, with Caiado 5%, Renan Santos 4%, Zema 3% and Augusto Cury 3%, and Lula 46% to Flávio 43% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). The comparison that counts is PoderData against itself, and there the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) gap did NOT move: it was 6pp on Jul 16 (40% to 34%) and it is 6pp now (41% to 35%), with the top two each gaining 1pp, inside the 2pp margin. The tightening only shows up if the ruler is swapped mid-measurement, comparing today's PoderData with yesterday's AtlasIntel, which gave 9.1pp. That is a house effect, not movement, and the panel does not add the two together. THE METHOD FINDING IS RENAN SANTOS, and it undoes yesterday's. On Jul 29 the panel recorded the distance between price and polling falling to 0.90pp, with AtlasIntel giving 7.8%. PoderData gives 4%, and the distance REOPENS to 4.45pp against his 8.45% price. Inside PoderData itself he FALLS from 6% to 4%, same house and same method, and the market went the same way in the place where it matters: the first-round second-place book COLLAPSED from 11.70% to 6.10%, a fall of 5.60pp, while the third-place book ROSE 0.50pp, to 62.00%. The money took Renan out of the runoff contest and pinned him into third place. Yesterday's convergence was a single-institute artifact, not a trend. REJECTION TIED: PoderData has Lula and Flávio at the SAME 49%, and the management rating gets worse, with poor or terrible at 47%, up 10pp against the institute's Jul 22 round. THE DAY'S INSTITUTIONAL AXIS is the PT at the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse): the Brazil of Hope Federation filed on Thursday a petition of more than 200 pages against a network of 31 profiles that, according to its claim, uses artificial intelligence to attack Lula, with 1,464,245 combined followers, 23,828 posts and an estimated reach of 10 million accounts, requesting removal of URLs, lifting of anonymity and demonetization. And the institutional market went the other way: impeachment of an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) justice FELL 0.25pp, to 3.10%, in a book of USD 83,000, undoing part of yesterday's rise. Total accumulated volume in the presidential market at USD 116.58M. Crossed with live Polymarket Jul 30, 20:08 UTC. The double-reading capture guard ran once and APPROVED with no divergence at all across the five books it covers, which had not happened since Jul 28: it blocked on both of the previous rounds. Every price goes in FIRM, with no declared range.

candidates.name: Lula
candidates.header: Polymarket 63.50% (up 1.00pp, vol USD 7.74M accumulated), 66 days to the election. Ties the top of the AFOS series for the third time, without exceeding it, and widens the gap over Flávio to +39.55pp. The day's polling, PoderData/Aya, gives 41% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) and 46% to 43% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), with the house's own gap flat at 6pp since Jul 16.
fortes: Returns to 63.50% and TIES the top of the AFOS series for the third time, set on Jul 26, Jul 28 and now Jul 30, with the gap over Flávio 0.25pp below the series maximum.
At PoderData he holds 41% to 35% in the first round, and the house's own gap has been flat at 6pp since Jul 16, meaning the polling reads as stability and not retreat.
Wins the PoderData runoff 46% to 43%, and it is the ninth consecutive round of national polls in which he leads in the second round.
Wins Ceará 55% to 22% in Thursday's Genial/Quaest, holding the Northeast lead the panel has been recording.
The PSB formalized on Jul 29 the nomination of Alckmin as running mate, with a coalition of PT, PCdoB, PV, PDT, PSol and Rede, and the PT national convention that formalizes him is set for Aug 2.
fracos: Personal approval FALLS to 43% against 49% disapproval, down 3pp and up 2pp against the institute's own Jul 22 round.
On the MANAGEMENT rating, poor or terrible goes to 47%, up 10pp inside the same house, the largest swing in a single indicator at any institute in this window.
The 3pp runoff lead fits inside the two margins added together, so PoderData describes a statistical tie and not a lead.
Loses Rio Grande do Sul in both rounds: 30% to 32% in the first and 35% to 40% in the runoff (Genial/Quaest).
Comes THIRD in Goiás, with 23%, behind Caiado (33%) and Flávio (27%).
candidates.analise: The day repeats the Jul 28 pattern: the price moved a full point and the polling evidence, read inside the same house, is flat. PoderData/Aya of Jul 30 (n=2,400, field Jul 26 to 29, 2pp margin, 95% confidence, BR-07845/2026, telephone on mobile and landline, 677 municipalities across the 27 states) has Lula 41% to Flávio 35% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) and 46% to 43% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). The comparison that counts is PoderData against itself, and there the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) gap did NOT move: it was 6pp on Jul 16 (40% to 34%) and it is 6pp now (41% to 35%), with the top two each gaining 1pp, inside the 2pp margin. The tightening only shows up if the ruler is swapped mid-measurement, comparing today's PoderData with yesterday's AtlasIntel, which gave 9.1pp. That is a house effect, not movement, and the panel does not add the two together. What the round brings that is new is not in voting intention, it is in evaluation: personal approval falls to 43% against 49% disapproval, down 3pp and up 2pp against the institute's Jul 22 round, and the MANAGEMENT rating gets sharply worse, with poor or terrible jumping to 47%, up 10pp. It is the worst management number the panel has recorded at any institute in this window, and it contrasts with yesterday's AtlasIntel, which brought 49.3% on the same indicator but with approval RISING. Two houses, two opposite signals in the same week, and the panel records both without arbitrating. REJECTION is the other record: 49% for Lula and 49% for Flávio, tied, when yesterday's AtlasIntel gave 49.4% against 52.9%. In the market, the 63.50% ties the top of the series without exceeding it, and the +39.55pp gap sits 0.25pp below the maximum. In Thursday's state polls, Genial/Quaest published ten states: Lula loses Rio Grande do Sul in both rounds, wins Ceará 55% to 22% and comes THIRD in Goiás, with 23%.

candidates.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
candidates.header: Polymarket 23.95% (flat, vol USD 7.71M accumulated). The run of four daily gains stopped. The gap widened because Lula rose, not because he fell. In the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) second-place book he reached 79.00%, up 0.50pp. PoderData has him at 35% in the first round and 43% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), with rejection at 49%, tied with Lula's.
fortes: Rejection measured by PoderData TIES with Lula's at 49%, when AtlasIntel of Jul 29 gave 52.9% against 49.4%: the asymmetry the panel had been recording did not appear in this reading.
RISES 0.50pp in the first-round second-place book, to 79.00%, his highest mark in that contract in the panel's tracking, with the market concentrating the second runoff slot in him.
Rises from 34% to 35% in the first round inside PoderData itself, against the Jul 16 round.
Leads Rio Grande do Sul in BOTH rounds: 32% to 30% in the first and 40% to 35% in the runoff (Genial/Quaest).
His 43% in the PoderData runoff sits 3pp from Lula, a difference that fits inside the two margins added together and constitutes a statistical tie.
fracos: The price was FLAT at 23.95% and the run of four consecutive daily closes on the rise, which had come from 22.90% on Jul 25, was broken.
The gap against him widened 1.00pp on the day, from +38.55pp to +39.55pp, and came within 0.25pp of the AFOS series maximum.
Still has NO running mate named, with the Aug 5 deadline less than a week away.

The petition filed by the Brazil of Hope Federation at the TSE on Thursday attributes to him, among other politicians, the boosting of content from the network of 31 profiles, a federation claim the panel has not independently verified.
Stayed put at 6.25% in the third-place book, without following the rise he had in the second-place one.
candidates.analise: The distinction that organizes his day is between a gap that widens by his own movement and one that widens by his opponent's, and today it was the second case: he stayed flat at 23.95% and the gap widened 1.00pp because Lula rose. The run of four daily closes on the rise, which had come from 22.90% on Jul 25, was broken without a fall. In the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) second-place sub-market he RISES 0.50pp and reaches 79.00% (vol USD 215,000), his highest mark in that book in the panel's tracking, and the counterpart to that is Renan Santos collapsing in the same book, from 11.70% to 6.10%: the market is concentrating in Flávio the probability of taking the second [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) slot. In the polling, PoderData brings him to 35% in the first round, against 34% from the house itself on Jul 16, and to 43% in the runoff, the same value as the institute's two previous rounds. The news is REJECTION: 49%, tied with Lula's. In every recent national poll, with the exception of Gerp of Jul 22, his rejection had come in equal to or above Lula's, and yesterday's AtlasIntel measured 52.9% against 49.4%. One reading does not undo the series, but the panel records that the asymmetry did not appear in this one. In the state polls, he leads Rio Grande do Sul 32% to 30% in the first round and 40% to 35% in the runoff, and sits second in Goiás, with 27%. The Aug 5 deadline for naming a running mate still stands.

candidates.name: Renan Santos
candidates.header: Polymarket 8.45% in the winner book (down 0.25pp, vol USD 8.59M accumulated). The number of the day is not that one: it is the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) second place, which COLLAPSED from 11.70% to 6.10%, a fall of 5.60pp, while third place rose 0.50pp, to 62.00%. And the new polling cuts him from 6% to 4% inside the same house.
fortes: The first-round third-place book ROSE 0.50pp, to 62.00%, and he remains the most likely name in that contract by a wide margin over Caiado, who has 25.50%.
Holds the largest accumulated volume among the competitive names in the presidential market, USD 8.59M, above Lula and Flávio.

Estadão recorded on Thursday that he is the candidate boosting the most ads against Lula AND against Flávio at the same time, which is consistent with a candidacy contesting third place rather than the polarization.
Still holds the third-highest price in the presidential book, ahead of the entire chasing pack.
fracos: The first-round second-place book COLLAPSED from 11.70% to 6.10%, a fall of 5.60pp in a contract of USD 1.09M, and it is the largest single move of the day anywhere in the panel.
The new polling cuts him from 6% to 4% inside PoderData ITSELF, same house and same method, the round's largest individual swing.
The distance between price and polling REOPENS from 0.90pp to 4.45pp, which undoes the convergence the panel recorded on Jul 29 based on a single survey.
Falls 0.25pp in the winner contract, to 8.45%, below every daily close of the past week in the AFOS series.
The spread between institutes has not resolved and still runs six points wide within the same month: 7.8% at AtlasIntel, 6% at Nexus, 5% at Indexa, 4% at PoderData and 3% at Datafolha.
candidates.analise: This is the entry the panel has to correct, and the correction is about yesterday's reading, not about a wrong number. On Jul 29 the panel recorded that the distance between his price and the polling had fallen to 0.90pp, and underlined that this time the narrowing came from the POLLING side, which had risen to 7.8% at AtlasIntel. One institute later, PoderData has him at 4% and the distance REOPENS to 4.45pp against his 8.45% price. More important than the comparison between houses: inside PoderData ITSELF he FALLS from 6% on Jul 16 to 4% now, same house, same telephone method, same 2pp margin, and that 2pp fall is the round's largest individual swing. The methodological conclusion is that yesterday's convergence was the artifact of one survey, and the panel undoes it rather than leaving it standing. The market moved the same way, and in exactly the place where the reading matters. The winner book gave up little, 0.25pp. The [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) second-place book COLLAPSED 5.60pp, from 11.70% to 6.10% (vol USD 1.09M). And the third-place book ROSE 0.50pp, to 62.00% (vol USD 164,000). Added together, the three moves say the same thing: the money did not take him out of the election, it reclassified him, removing his chance of contesting the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) and consolidating him as the third-placed name. The spread between institutes, which the panel has been recording for weeks, still has not resolved and now runs six points wide within the same month: 7.8%, 6%, 5%, 4% and 3%. In parallel, Estadão recorded on Thursday that he is the candidate boosting the most ads against BOTH front-runners at the same time, which is consistent with a candidacy contesting third place rather than the polarization.

candidates.name: Caiado / Haddad / Zema
candidates.header: Polymarket: Caiado 2.55% (up 0.20pp, vol USD 5.20M), Jair 1.05% (flat), Zema 0.55% (down 0.20pp), Haddad 0.15% (down 0.10pp). In the polling, Caiado rises from 4% to 5% inside PoderData and LEADS Goiás with 33%, ahead of Flávio and Lula.
candidates.subtitle: Jul 30, 66 days out: the chasing pack split into two signals. Caiado is the only name in the panel where price and polling rose together, going to 5% at PoderData and 2.55% in the market, and he leads Goiás with 33%. Zema fell on both, from 4% to 3% in the polling and 0.20pp in price, to 0.55%. Haddad remains outside the main first-round scenario and gave up 0.10pp, to 0.15%.

caiado.label: CAIADO (PSD), presidential Poly 2.55% (up 0.20pp, vol USD 5.20M) | [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) third place 25.50% (flat, vol USD 37,000) | second place 0.90% (up 0.30pp) | candidacy made official on Jul 26, with Kassab as running mate | latest national poll: PoderData Jul 30, first round 5%
caiado.fortes: He is the only name in the panel where price and polling moved together today, and both upward. In the polling, PoderData returns him to 5%, up 1pp inside the house itself against the Jul 16 round, and that comes 24 hours after AtlasIntel had cut him to 3.1%, half the 6% at BTG/Nexus. The divergence about him therefore did NOT close in favour of the low reading: 6%, 5% and 3.1% are all still live. In the market, he rises 0.20pp in the winner book, to 2.55%, adding up to 0.65pp over two sessions, from 1.90% on Jul 28, and rises 0.30pp in the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) second-place book, to 0.90%. And the state figure of the day is the strongest thing in the entry: Genial/Quaest has him LEADING Goiás with 33%, ahead of Flávio (27%) and Lula (23%).
caiado.fracos: The caveat is about size and comes before the reading: 5% of polling with a 2pp margin and a 2.55% price are different quantities measuring different things, and matching direction confirms nothing. The [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) third-place contract stayed FLAT at 25.50%, meaning the day's rise did not show up in the book where he actually contests position, and Renan Santos rose 0.50pp in that same contract, to 62.00%. In the state where he leads, disapproval of his government is 59% in the same survey, which separates local strength from judgement of his management. And the level remains low: 2.55% in the presidential contract against 63.50% for the front-runner.

haddad.label: HADDAD (PT), presidential Poly 0.15% (down 0.10pp) | [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) second place 0.85% (down 0.30pp) | not tested in the main first-round scenario by the national polls, because he is running for governor of São Paulo
haddad.fortes: The record of the day is one of absence: PoderData does not test him in any scenario, neither [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) nor [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), and so he has no new polling in this round. His most recent favourable reading is still AtlasIntel of Jul 29, in one of the two runoff scenarios WITHOUT Lula, where he appears with 44.3% against 43.7% for Flávio, a statistical tie inside the 1pp margin.
haddad.fracos: He fell in both contracts where he appears: 0.10pp in the winner book, to 0.15%, and 0.30pp in the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) second-place book, to 0.85%. It is the exact inverse of the crossed signal the panel recorded on Jul 29, when he had risen in the placing book and stayed flat in the winner one. The interpretive caveat stands and needs saying plainly: he is NOT a presidential candidate, he is running for governor of São Paulo, and the scenario that favours him is a polling hypothesis and not a candidacy in progress.

zema.label: ZEMA (Novo), presidential Poly 0.55% (down 0.20pp, vol USD 4.57M) | [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) third place 4.50% | PoderData Jul 30: first round 3%, against 4% from the house itself on Jul 16 | candidacy made official by Novo on Jul 27, still with NO running mate, deadline Aug 5
zema.fortes: He remains the third-highest price in the chasing pack in the presidential contract and holds 4.50% in the first-round third-place book, ahead of every name in the pack except Caiado. He has been official for Novo since Jul 27, which distinguishes him from names the institutes still treat as hypothetical.
zema.fracos: He is the only name in the panel that fell on BOTH measures on the same day: from 4% to 3% inside PoderData and 0.20pp in the market, to 0.55%, giving back exactly what he had gained the day before. He is also the second institute in a row to measure him below 3%, after the 2.8% from AtlasIntel of Jul 29, which additionally had him losing the national runoff to Lula 48.6% to 39.6%. He still has no running mate, with the Aug 5 deadline less than a week away. A caveat on the series, and it is a big one: his maximum in the AFOS series is 10.10%, from Apr 26, so 0.55% sits at a little over a twentieth of that level.

candidates.analise: Caiado is the only name in the chasing pack where price and polling rose together today, and he does it after a bad round. Yesterday's AtlasIntel cut him to 3.1%, half the 6% at BTG/Nexus, and the panel recorded that the third measurement had landed on the low reading. PoderData returns him to 5%, up 1pp inside the house itself against Jul 16, and the divergence about him did NOT close: 6% at Nexus, 5% at PoderData and 3.1% at AtlasIntel are all still live. Governing with poor ratings and leading the presidential race in your own state are compatible facts, and the panel records both without turning one into the other. HADDAD is still not tested in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) by the institutes and falls 0.10pp in the market, to 0.15%. JAIR does not move, at 1.05%, and is the only one in the group whose price is unchanged.

quadroComparativo.t: FALLS 0.20pp in the presidential contract, to 0.55%, and stands at 4.50% in the first-round third-place book. He gives back exactly what he had gained the day before.
quadroComparativo.s: He fell on both measures on the same day, polling and price, and is the only name in the panel where that happened. A caveat on the series, and it is a big one: his maximum in the AFOS series is 10.10%, from Apr 26, so 0.55% sits at a little over a twentieth of that level, and 0.20pp moves in that range carry very little information.

quadroComparativo.p: No polling. Market on the impeachment of an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) justice before 2027.
quadroComparativo.t: FALLS 0.25pp to 3.10%, meaning the price went the OPPOSITE way to the day's institutional accumulation, undoing part of yesterday's 0.55pp rise.
quadroComparativo.s: A decisive methodological caveat, and it comes before any reading: with USD 83,000 in accumulated volume against USD 116.58M in the presidential market, 0.25pp in that book is very little money. The day's context was one of accumulation: the Brazil of Hope Federation filed at the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) a petition of more than 200 pages against a network of profiles that, according to its claim, uses artificial intelligence against Lula, and it is the third day in a row in which the institutional axis is the use of AI in campaigning. On Jul 29 the price followed the accumulation; today it contradicts it. Two days, two directions, a net move of 0.30pp up. The honest reading is that this book is not big enough to respond to the news, and reading cause into it in either direction would be building narrative on noise.

cruzamento: THE CROSSING OF JUL 30 has only one question, and it is the same as Jul 28: why the price moves a full point on a day when the polling, read properly, is flat. Lula RISES 1.00pp and returns to 63.50%, which TIES the top of the AFOS series for the third time (Jul 26, Jul 28 and Jul 30) without exceeding it on any of the three. Flávio stays at 23.95%, flat, breaking four consecutive daily gains. The gap widens from +38.55pp to +39.55pp and sits 0.25pp below the series maximum, the +39.80pp of Jul 26. Recording that the gap widened by movement on one side only is mandatory: there was no repricing of Flávio's candidacy today. THE POLLING. PoderData/Aya of Jul 30 (n=2,400, field Jul 26 to 29, 2pp margin, 95% confidence, BR-07845/2026, telephone on mobile and landline, 677 municipalities across the 27 states) has Lula 41% to Flávio 35% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), with Caiado 5%, Renan Santos 4%, Zema 3% and Augusto Cury 3%, plus 5% blank or void and 4% who did not answer, and Lula 46% to Flávio 43% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). The comparison that counts is PoderData against itself, and there the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) gap did NOT move: it was 6pp on Jul 16 (40% to 34%) and it is 6pp now (41% to 35%), with the top two each gaining 1pp, inside the 2pp margin. The tightening only shows up if the ruler is swapped mid-measurement, comparing today's PoderData with yesterday's AtlasIntel, which gave 9.1pp. That is a house effect, not movement, and the panel does not add the two together. The temptation was to write that the polling tightened, because PoderData's 6pp against AtlasIntel's 9.1pp looks like tightening. It is not: it is the same level difference between the two houses that the panel has been recording since Jul 16, when PoderData contradicted Quaest with Lula IDENTICAL and the whole disagreement on Flávio. WHAT CHANGED IN THE POLLING was the evaluation, not the voting intention. Lula's personal approval falls to 43% against 49% disapproval, and the MANAGEMENT rating gets sharply worse: poor or terrible goes to 47%, up 10pp against the institute's Jul 22 round, and good or very good sits at 34%, with 16% fair. It is the worst management number in the window, and it comes 24 hours after AtlasIntel measured approval RISING 1.7pp. Two houses, two opposite signals in the same week, on the same indicator. The panel records both and does not arbitrate which is right, because it has no way to. And REJECTION TIED at 49% for Lula and 49% for Flávio, when yesterday AtlasIntel gave 49.4% against 52.9%. The asymmetry the panel had been calling a structural constraint on Flávio's candidacy did not appear in this reading. One round does not undo the series, but it is on the record. THE METHOD FINDING IS RENAN SANTOS, and it undoes yesterday's finding. On Jul 29 the panel wrote that the distance between price and polling had fallen to 0.90pp and that, for the first time, the narrowing had come from the POLLING side, which had risen to 7.8% at AtlasIntel. PoderData has him at 4%, and the distance REOPENS to 4.45pp. Inside PoderData ITSELF he falls from 6% to 4%, same house and same method, the round's largest individual swing. And the market went the same way, in the place where it means something: the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) second-place book COLLAPSED from 11.70% to 6.10%, a fall of 5.60pp in a book of USD 1.09M, while the third-place book ROSE 0.50pp, to 62.00%. The money did not eliminate him, it reclassified him. The spread between institutes has not resolved and runs six points wide within the same month: 7.8%, 6%, 5%, 4% and 3%. CAIADO is the only name where price and polling rose together: 5% at PoderData, up 1pp inside the house, and 2.55% in the market, up 0.20pp. The divergence about him is still open at three levels, and the day's state poll brings the round's sharpest mismatch: Genial/Quaest has him LEADING Goiás with 33%, ahead of Flávio (27%) and Lula (23%), in the same survey where disapproval of his state government is 59%. THE INSTITUTIONAL AXIS is the PT at the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse). The Brazil of Hope Federation filed on Thursday a petition of more than 200 pages against a network of 31 profiles that, ACCORDING TO THE FEDERATION'S CLAIM, uses artificial intelligence to attack Lula, totalling 1,464,245 followers, 23,828 posts and an estimated reach of 10 million accounts, requesting removal of URLs, lifting of anonymity and demonetization, and attributing boosting to Flávio and other politicians (Metrópoles, CNN Brasil, Migalhas). It is the third day in a row in which artificial intelligence in campaigning is the institutional axis, after the 48 hours Moraes gave on Jul 28 and the reply from Jair's defence on Jul 29. And the market went the OPPOSITE way to the accumulation: impeachment of an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) justice FELL 0.25pp, to 3.10% (vol USD 83,000), undoing part of yesterday's 0.55pp rise. Across two days, 0.55pp up and 0.25pp down in a book of USD 83,000 is noise, and the panel records it without building narrative. IN THE PARTY CALENDAR, the PSB formalized on Jul 29 the nomination of Geraldo Alckmin as running mate on Lula's ticket, in Brasília, with the coalition including PT, PCdoB, PV, PDT, PSol and Rede, and the PT national convention that formalizes Lula is set for Aug 2, in São Paulo. TWO THIN BOOKS MOVED A LOT and deserve the same caveat. In the Senate, the PL FELL 5.50pp, from 71.00% to 65.50%, and the MDB rose 0.60pp, to 18.20%, in a book totalling USD 292,000, with USD 258,000 concentrated in the PL itself. In inflation, the modal band is still 5.00% to 5.49%, at 38.30%, but the 4.50% to 4.99% band fell from 34.90% to 32.50% and the 5.50% to 5.99% band rose from 4.10% to 5.80%, in a book of USD 81,000 that is NOT covered by the double-reading capture guard. A large move in a small book is a record, not a signal. IN THE PRESS, Lula said nobody is going to stick their nose into Brazil's elections, criticizing the United States and Argentina, and Estadão recorded that Renan Santos is the candidate boosting the most ads against BOTH front-runners at the same time. A NOTE ON CAPTURE, and this time it is short. The double-reading capture guard ran once and APPROVED with no divergence at all across the five books it covers, which had not happened since Jul 28: it blocked on both of the previous rounds. Every price goes in FIRM, with no declared range. Total accumulated volume in the presidential market at USD 116.58M.
